data.name: Rise of Industry
data.detailed_description:
UPCOMING SEQUEL


Acerca do jogo





Rise of Industry is a strategic tycoon game where you build and manage your growing industrial empire in a living, breathing, and procedurally generated world set in the 1930s that is constantly evolving and adapting to your playstyle.

As a budding entrepreneur, you will build factories, construct efficient production lines, move raw materials, produce finished goods, and arrange trade with the world's developing cities, providing them with the resources they need to flourish - for as they grow and prosper, so do you.

However, it won’t always be a smooth ride to magnate status. Random business events and stock auctions will keep you on your toes, all while A.I. rivals compete for market share and look for ways to grow and exploit enemy weaknesses - beware of the hostile takeover.

Designed with an eye towards both accessibility and depth, Rise of Industry has enough strategic complexity and replayability to satisfy the most experienced fans of the genre, while its simple-to-understand mechanics ensure that new players will love it as well.





  • Experience tailored for every player - Specialise in just trading, production, gathering or any combination and research your way to bigger and better things.
  • Bid for contracts to get the upper-hand over your rivals.
  • Produce over 150 individual products, managing every step along the way from raw material to end product. Only the highly skilled entrepreneur will complete the complex production chains and take items such as cars, computers and other luxury products to market.
  • Build and manage a solid transportation network to enable the efficient transfer of goods via plentiful trucks, speedy trains and high capacity airships.
  • Be prepared for fierce competition – Advanced town and city A.I., make for an intelligent and changing game world so you won’t be the only one looking for the best deal.
  • Town personalities – adapt a suitable approach for every town or face their economic backlash.
  • Huge, procedurally generated maps mean that you’ll always have room to expand your empire, whether in testing scenarios or sandbox mode where imagination is your only limit.
  • Be quick to adapt to the current business climate with contracts and random events keeping you on your toes and cash flowing in.
  • Balance environmental impact with productivity. Churn out the products at the expense of nature, or be a conscientious industrialist, balancing the delicate lay of the land with your hunger for profit.

As an early 20th-Century industrialist, grow your empire & adapt to an ever-changing business landscape with unexpected events that could lead to boom…or bust.

reviews.review:
5/10 - "Rise of Industry" is a tycoon game, that would be best described by what it isn't, than by what it actually is. It is not a logistics-management game, as the logistics part of the game is highly limited. It is not a factory-builder, as the production chains are very simple. It is not a city-builder, as the demands of the citizens are only represented by the options of products you can sell at their shop to make money, without any repercussions for not selling enough of them in a given timeframe or any at all. Simply put, it is an easy and relaxing tycoon game, that fits best for people, that never played tycoon games before and want to get their feet wet. It is definitely not the kind of game I would normally play, as I am not really into tycoon games and I expected something different, but that is more my fault, than the games fault. However, what i was actually able to experience make me not want to play any other tycoon game, if all of them are like that.

[h1] Pros [/h1]
[list]
    [*]The game doesn't really force you into a specific kind of product to produce and sell, only depending on what resources you have on your part of the map. You can decide to only sell food items or clothing, and still make a good amount of money. 
    [*]Each type of product also has an "end-game product", which acts as the win-condition for completely producing it. So every player can decide to pursue a different kind of product to win the game, instead of all player going after the same thing.
    [*]If you do not want to deal with calculating how to satisfy the demand of the shops with the different production times of the farms and factories, the game has a "Simplified Production Time" option, that will round all production times up or down to fall in any of the 15 / 30 / 45 days production times. This will make the game that much more enjoyable for players that seek a more relaxing and zen-like tycoon.
    [*]The demand system I both like and dislike. You do not have to fully supply a product to a shop for a city to grow. However, you are being punished for supplying exactly as much as they demand, by its price going down. The game doesn't give you good, if any, indicators of those things.
[/list]
[h1] Cons [/h1]
[list]
    [*]The logistics part of the game just ... exist and nothing more. There is no lane-management, lane-prioritization, traffic lights or similar features. Aside from "normal road" and "one-way" road, there is really no other way to influence traffic. Unless you want to waste valuable space for complex road layouts, you just learn to except the occasional traffic congestion.
    [*]Another issue with the logistics, is not being able to transport more than one resources at the same time using trains, ships or airships. Every item in the warehouse will get it's own separate train and trip, which is highly inefficient, especially when multiple low-quantity items need to be transported a long distance.
    [*]There is no easy or direct way to figure out, how profitable any given items is that you produce. It takes a lot of manual calculations, which sour the experience of playing the game.
    [*]The UI can be frustrating at time. The factories UI has their information spread over multiple tabs, and finding the right one takes quite some time to get used to. For some reason when selecting a building, it always open the second tab first that has the least important information, instead of maybe the first tab (that has the production overview / the most important information for a factory?). When looking at an existing transportation route of a building, the exporting and importing buildings are not highlighted on the map and the route is barely visible & doesn't show you the trucks that are currently en-route to the importing building. 
    [*]There is only two real types of roads: "Dirt Road" and "Urban Road". Why is there no "Highway" type road for faster transportation? Since you only have the "Urban Road" for most of the playtime, the movement speed of the trucks never improve and will always feel the same kind of "slow".
    [*]The description of the warehouse options are not transparent enough. What does "wait until full" mean? "Wait until the warehouse is full" or "Wait until the truck / train / ship / airship is full"? You have to experiment to figure that out. The warehouse doesn't show you the max capacity of any of the vehicle options, at least not that I could find it, which further complicated the earlier confusion with the "wait until full" option. When the game says "warehouse full", it is not the entire warehouse that is full, but only the storage for a specific item, every other item can still be stored, but the game doesn't tell you that or make it obvious in any way.
    [*] The Decontamination / Cleaning buildings to not have a visible radius for their effect, neither before nor after placing the building. Because of this, you are forced to just experiment to figure out it's max range. These are the only buildings that have this issue to my knowledge.
[/list]
